artifacts.summary: Verifies the dispatch's incident/taxonomy claims, reconciles the fix set to 20 files/22 edit sites, finds that manifest routing_agents membership does not predict canonical-vocabulary use, finds orchestrate-recover-outcome.sh's success arm is too narrow for several already-designed non-canonical success vocabularies, and settles all five open design questions (lint scope via a new recorded-exclusion list, pipe-placeholder handling incl. grant-agent's bespoke case, vocabulary-extraction target/name, runtime-wiring deferred out of scope, and file_scope for the plan).

memory_candidates.content: When auditing agent-contract status vocabularies across extensions, manifest.json routing_agents membership does NOT predict canonical-vocabulary use: several registered research/plan/implement phase-routing targets (filetypes-router-agent, slidev-assembly-agent, legal-analysis-agent, project-agent, grant-agent) intentionally use non-canonical terminal status values. A lint restricting scope to 'lifecycle-dispatch agents derived from routing tables' will wrongly include these. Use an explicit recorded-exclusion list (mirroring lint-agent-contracts.sh's EXCLUDED_ARTIFACTS_TEMPLATE_RELATIVE_PATHS) instead.

orchestrate-recover-outcome.sh's success case arm (researched|planned|implemented) is narrower than the full set of intentionally-designed per-extension success statuses (e.g. filetypes-router-agent's 'converted', slidev-assembly-agent's 'assembled', legal-analysis-agent's 'consulted'). Any of these agents dispatched under orchestrator_mode:true would have a genuinely successful outcome misclassified as STATUS_NOT_SUCCESS today -- the same defect class as an agent wrongly writing status:'completed', just triggered by an intentional non-canonical value. Widening the recovery arm's acceptance set should be resolved before wiring any stricter rejection validator (e.g. validate-return-meta.sh) into the same read path, or the validator will newly break these working agents.
